title: JKJAAC appeals for end to military operation in Rawalakot
seoTitle: Rawalakot JKJAAC appeals against military action

tea.why: Protesters are demonstrating against soaring electricity tariffs, wheat subsidy cuts, heavy taxation, and government failure on a 38-point charter.
tea.want: Demonstrators demand political, economic, and governance reforms, an end to military operations, and accountability for deaths.
tea.changed: Nov 9: JKJAAC appealed directly to Pakistan Army Chief Asim Munir to halt military operations following a November 5 crackdown in Rawalakot.

summary: The Jammu Kashmir Joint Awami Action Committee (JKJAAC) has appealed to Pakistan Army Chief Asim Munir to end military operations in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, particularly following a November 5 security crackdown in Rawalakot to clear protest camps. Protests expanded across the region, with demonstrators expressing grievances over soaring electricity tariffs, wheat subsidy cuts, heavy taxation, and unmet demands from a 38-point charter of rights. The JKJAAC reported that security forces utilized excessive force, including heavy weapons and drones, during the operations. Committee representatives accused the authorities of attacking peaceful demonstrators and mass detentions, while Pakistani police accused protest participants of attacking law enforcement personnel. The committee requested the immediate withdrawal of military personnel, accountability for casualties, and a return to meaningful dialogue.
organizers: Jammu Kashmir Joint Awami Action Committee (JKJAAC)
demands: End to military operations in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir
Withdrawal of military personnel from affected areas
Accountability and justice for killed protesters
Fulfillment of the 38-point charter of rights
response: Pakistani security forces launched an operation to clear protest camps using heavy weapons and drones, while police accused members of the protest movement of attacking law enforcement personnel, according to sources.

injuries.text: around 200 were injured in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir's Rawalakot and neighbouring areas

deaths.text: more than 150 people have died in connection with the protests

updates.text: Pakistani security forces launched an operation in Rawalakot to clear protest camps, resulting in reported deaths and injuries.
Reports indicated civil unrest and crackdowns expanded to Muzaffarabad amid rising living costs and military actions.
The JKJAAC issued a formal appeal to Pakistan Army Chief Asim Munir demanding an end to military operations.
